source_name: ČNB – Zprávy o výkonu dohledu nad finančním trhem (annual supervision reports)
why_relevant: Annual reports (archive spanning ~2010 onwards) with counts of licensed entities per category, licensing and sanctioning activity in the payments area, and supervisory priorities. The best single benchmark series for sizing and trending the CZ payments competitor set year over year.

source_name: ČNB – Statistika platebního styku / komentář (payment statistics)
why_relevant: Official harmonised payment statistics: cards issued, POS terminals deployed by CZ acquirers, accounts, transaction counts by payment service and by terminal type. The authoritative denominator for any CZ payments market sizing and the benchmark against which vendor/acquirer share claims are tested (e.g. ~285k POS terminals at end-2025, >16.6m cards mid-2025 per ČNB commentary).

source_name: ČNB – ARAD systém časových řad (time series database)
why_relevant: Public time-series database behind ČNB statistics, with per-report parameterised URLs and export. Gives structured, downloadable history for payments, cards, terminals and banking-sector aggregates instead of PDF snapshots.

source_name: ČNB – Seznam účastníků systému CERTIS + Seznam účastníků okamžitých plateb
why_relevant: Versioned lists of direct/indirect participants in the CZ interbank clearing system CERTIS and, separately, of instant-payments participants. This is the operational payments infrastructure map: who clears directly, who piggybacks, and which institutions have gone live on instant payments — a strong proxy for payment-platform vendor projects and partnerships.

source_name: ČNB – Číselník kódů platebního styku v ČR (ČKPS / bank codes) a Číselníky, seznamy, registry
why_relevant: The bank-code codelist is the join key between institution names, IBANs and clearing participation, and the hub page also carries the list of payment systems, foreign settlement-system participants, and comparison-website operators under §202 of the Payments Act. Indispensable for entity resolution across all other CZ payments sources.

source_name: ČNB – Ostatní seznamy (other supervisory lists: payment systems, covered-bond issuers, comparison sites)
why_relevant: Long tail of niche but high-signal official lists: 'Seznam platebních systémů', foreign settlement/payment-system participants, operators of comparison websites under §202 of the Payments Act, and the list of activities under the limited-network exclusion (which enumerates closed-loop/gift-card style payment schemes normally invisible in registers).

source_name: ČNB – Upozornění pro veřejnost / Upozornění ČNB na aktivity (public warnings, unauthorised providers)
why_relevant: Names entities operating without ČNB authorisation or misrepresenting ČNB approval. Useful as the negative-space complement to the register: it identifies grey-market payments/investment actors and helps validate that an unfamiliar 'fintech' is not in fact unlicensed.

source_name: ČNB – Stanoviska k regulaci finančního trhu (regulatory opinions, incl. PSD2 / payments scope)
why_relevant: Numbered supervisory opinions (RSYYYY-NN) interpreting the Payments Act — e.g. 2025 opinions on minimum user experience for payment-initiation services and prohibited obstacles for TPPs, and on whether corporate central payment/collection hubs fall under the Act. These set the supervisory benchmark that shapes what banks and their vendors must build, and flag where enforcement pressure will land next.

source_name: ČNB – DORA / digitální provozní odolnost finančního trhu (+ SDAT reporting)
why_relevant: DORA obliges every CZ financial entity to maintain and submit to ČNB a 'registr informací' listing all ICT third-party service providers and contractual arrangements — i.e. a regulator-held, structured map of exactly which vendors serve which Czech banks and payment institutions. The submissions themselves are not public, but ČNB's templates, webinars and reporting guidance define the vendor-relationship data model and are the best available public window onto it.

source_name: ČNB – Informační povinnosti subjektů finančního trhu / Co nového v dohledu
why_relevant: Enumerates the reporting obligations each licence category owes ČNB — which tells you what data exists about each competitor, in what granularity and cadence, and therefore what may become publicly derivable. The companion 'Co nového v dohledu' feed is the running change-log of supervisory expectations.

source_name: EBA – Central register of payment and electronic money institutions under PSD2
why_relevant: EU-level aggregation of national registers, live since 18 March 2019, downloadable in bulk and free to search. It gives the CZ subset (reported as ~201 entities in one third-party mirror) in a normalised cross-border schema, and crucially captures passporting: which foreign PIs/EMIs/TPPs are notified into CZ and which CZ entities passport out. Complements JERRS rather than replacing it — CZ TPP operation requires both EBA registration and a CZ notification in JERRS.

source_name: ÚOHS – Sbírky rozhodnutí a spojování soutěžitelů (competition authority)
why_relevant: Merger notifications and competition decisions covering CZ banking/payments — e.g. a ČSOB joint-control notification, an assessment of an ATM-sharing arrangement between several Czech banks, and a decision on the 'vklad na kartu' banking service. Merger and cooperation filings are one of the few sources that document bank–bank and bank–fintech partnerships and market-share reasoning in detail before they are announced commercially. Also published as an open dataset in the national open-data catalogue.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR – Platební služby a vypořádání obchodů (legislation, consultations)
why_relevant: MF ČR, not ČNB, owns the Payments Act (zákon č. 370/2017 Sb.) and runs the public consultations. Consultation dossiers and their published evaluations (e.g. the 2022 PSD2/ZPS evaluation) contain named submissions from banks, fintechs and industry associations — an unusually direct read on which actors exist, what they are building, and who allies with whom. Also the source for the digital-finance act adapting DORA/MiCA (zákon č. 32/2025 Sb.).

source_name: Financni-subjekty.penize.cz – mirror of ČNB regulated-entity lists
why_relevant: Commercial re-publication of the ČNB register in a far more scrapable HTML form than JERRS, useful as a fallback or cross-check when JERRS/open-data access is awkward. Secondary source: never authoritative, may lag, and licensing for reuse is unclear — treat ČNB as the system of record.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Tiskové zprávy (press room)
why_relevant: Primary owned channel of the largest CZ retail bank; announces new branch/tech formats, AI deployments, George digital banking milestones and occasionally names technology partners. Date-pathed URLs (/2025/11/12/...) make crawling and dedup straightforward.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Zprávy z banky
why_relevant: Secondary owned news stream, lighter/product-oriented than the formal press room; often carries digital-product and app-release notes that never become formal press releases.

source_name: Erste Developer Portal (Česká spořitelna API/dev portal)
why_relevant: Bank-owned developer portal exposing the API product catalogue (PSD2 AIS/PIS/CoF plus proprietary APIs), sandbox and changelogs. API surface and its evolution is a strong indirect signal of the underlying platform/vendor stack and of open-banking partnerships.

source_name: Komerční banka – Pro investory / Novinky (IR news)
why_relevant: KB is listed on PSE, so IR disclosures are the richest CZ source on IT transformation economics. The KB Change 2025 programme, the new digital bank and the associated core-banking decision were disclosed here; IR releases also carry transformation cost/capex figures that press releases omit.

source_name: Komerční banka – konsolidovaná výroční zpráva (annual report PDFs)
why_relevant: Annual reports carry the outsourcing / material-supplier and operational-risk sections plus intangible-asset and IT investment notes — exactly the vendor-dependency disclosures absent from press releases. The 2020 report explicitly documents the KB Change programme.

source_name: ČSOB – Povinně uveřejňované informace (mandatory disclosures / annual reports)
why_relevant: Central hub for ČSOB's statutory annual and half-year reports (2025 report published 2026-04-23). Annual reports are the only owned place where ČSOB discloses IT investment, outsourcing and group-level (KBC) technology dependencies.

source_name: Raiffeisenbank CZ – Tiskové zprávy (press room)
why_relevant: Well-structured, year/quarter-pathed owned press room. Publishes mobile-banking releases, digital-service developments and annual-report summaries; RBI FinTech Scouts participation surfaces here, which is a pointer to partnership pipelines.

source_name: Raiffeisenbank CZ – Výroční zprávy (annual financial reports)
why_relevant: Annual financial report PDFs carry digitalisation narrative, IT investment and outsourcing/operational-risk disclosures for a bank enlarged by the Equa bank merger — migrations of that scale are documented here rather than in press releases.

source_name: MONETA Money Bank – Investor Relations (investors.moneta.cz)
why_relevant: MONETA is PSE-listed and runs a full IR site with financial results, annual reports, mandatory disclosures and results presentations/webcasts. Digital-transformation spend, cloud migration and vendor dependencies are addressed in the results decks and Q&A more candidly than in press releases.

source_name: Air Bank – Konsolidovaná výroční zpráva (annual reports, PDF archive)
why_relevant: Air Bank (PPF/Home Credit group) publishes a long, directly linkable run of consolidated annual report PDFs (2016-2025). These disclose R&D spend on banking technology (CZK 457m in 2025 per reporting) and digital-service priorities — rare quantitative IT signal for a non-listed CZ bank.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia – Výroční a pololetní zprávy
why_relevant: Bank-hosted annual and half-year report PDFs under a stable /content/dam/ document tree. Reports cover group technology programmes localised to CZ/SK and outsourcing arrangements with UniCredit Services (intra-group IT provider) — a distinctive vendor pattern worth tracking.

source_name: Partners Banka – Pro média (press room)
why_relevant: Newest CZ bank (launched 2024) built greenfield on a modern stack; its own media page and product launches (e.g. multicurrency account) are the closest thing to a public build log of a fresh core-banking/mobile stack. High value for greenfield vendor selection intelligence.

source_name: Trinity Bank – Pro média / tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: Owned press room of a small SAB-group bank; publishes results and occasional digital-service news. Low volume but the only owned channel for this actor, and small banks buy packaged core/mobile solutions whose vendors are sometimes named.

source_name: Fio banka – O nás / organizational and corporate disclosures
why_relevant: Fio is notable for building its own banking software in-house (Fio's own IT arm), so its owned pages and reports are the only evidence of an insourced-stack outlier in the CZ market — an important negative datapoint for vendor addressable-market work.
